title: Soft watermarks and memory contracts for GPU slice headroom
creator: Avery Cole
description: Problem: OOMs and tail latency spikes occur when continuous batching and KV cache growth compete with weight/activation residency. Current static reserve policies either waste GPU capacity or cause hard OOMs during request bursts. Goal: introduce a soft-watermark / contract-based memory slicing system that provides predictable headroom for incoming requests while allowing opportunistic use of slack memory for KV and activations.
acceptance_criteria: Define soft and hard watermark semantics at per-tenant slice level and integrate with scheduler
Expose a memory contract API so request router can reserve headroom atomically before batching
Demonstrate >= 60% reduction in faculty OOMs on multi-tenant synthetic workload  (95th percentile over 24h), without increasing mean token cost by >5%
Fall back to graceful eviction (KV-first, then activation offload) with telemetry when soft->hard watermark crossing happens
End-to-end integration tests and chaos test that triggers KV runaway and validates safe rollback paths
tasks: Design: document watermark model and contract lifecycle (Avery)
Runtime: implement per-GPU slice soft/hard watermarks + atomic reserve API (Diego)
Router: add pre-batch reserve call and backpressure response code path (Priya)
KV: implement prioritized TTL/age based scavenge and eviction metrics (Lin)
Benchmarks: synthetic multi-tenant runner and Grafana dashboard (SRE)
E2E: chaos test that simulates KV runaway, activation spikes, and concurrent heavy batching (QA)
Docs: RFC and operator playbook for tuning watermarks (Avery)
design_notes: Soft watermark = warning threshold where components start yielding opportunistic capacity (KV trim, early activation offload). Hard watermark = enforced cap where new reservations must be rejected or deferred.

Contracts represent a transient reservation (amount, ttl, priority) that can be atomically acquired and released. Contracts are decoupled from tenant quotas so we can have short-lived burst reservations.

We will use a small in-GPU memory ledger object with lock-free counters to track weights, reserved_headroom, kv_resident, activation_resident. Ledger values are periodically exported to control-plane telemetry for cross-GPU coordination.

Reservation API must be latency-inexpensive: try_reserve(size, ttl, priority) returns success/failure and an optional suggested backoff. Router will call try_reserve immediately before entering a batch window.
When soft watermark crossed: trigger asynchronous KV compaction and signal scheduler to bias future batches towards smaller batch sizes until soft watermark resolves.

When hard watermark crossed: synchronous admission control — reject low-priority contracts, attempt immediate KV scavenging, then eviction of the oldest KV segments. Activation offload to host memory is last resort and must preserve correctness for cached KV (checkpointing ongoing requests).
Trade-offs: more aggressive soft-watermark trimming reduces OOM risk but hurts throughput. We'll tune via experiments and surface operator knobs (soft_delta_pct, eviction_grace_ms).

Compatibility: must work with quantized weights and model-slicing; contracts operate on bytes not semantic object types. Storage accounting will convert activations/KV objects into estimated bytes using existing estimator functions.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on contract model and hardware ledger design. Action: runtime to prototype ledger counters + test harness (Diego)
2026-02-22: Prototype ledger implemented. Microbenchmark shows try_reserve latency median 27us on A100, p99 120us (includes atomic update + local check). Good baseline for router integration.
2026-03-01: KV scavenger added heuristics to prioritize segments by last-access + estimated reclaimable bytes. In synthetic KV growth test this reclaimed 45% of runaway KV within 60s.

2026-03-05: Router integration branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/814). Router calls try_reserve before entering continuous batch windows. Observed admission backpressure during spike tests.

2026-03-08: Multi-tenant benchmark (12 tenants, mixed model sizes, bursty traffic) ran for 12h. Results: OOM count reduced by 78% vs baseline; however tail token latency increased ~8% during peak bursts. Next step: tune soft_delta_pct and eviction thresholds to trade latency vs OOMs.

2026-03-11: Chaos test triggered KV runaway + simultaneous large batch. System entered soft->hard path and successfully evicted oldest KV segments; one low-priority contract was rejected per policy. No customer requests failed with CORRUPT state; only increased latency observed.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reservation API adds latency to request path. Mitigation: keep try_reserve microbenchmark < 200us p99 and provide async pre-warm for high-frequency clients.
Risk: Aggressive evictions reduce cache hit rate and increase model compute. Mitigation: prioritize eviction of stale/low-value KV entries using access frequency and value-size heuristics.

Risk: Cross-GPU coordination could become a bottleneck if all GPUs try global compaction. Mitigation: use staggered compaction windows and local-first heuristics; promote global compaction only when local measures fail.
Risk: Wrong size estimates for activations/KV cause over/under reservation. Mitigation: add calibration job that periodically re-trains estimator parameters from sampled telemetry.
Risk: Operator complexity. Mitigation: ship safe defaults and an operator playbook with tuning knobs and regression rollback steps.
experiments_and_metrics: Synthetic setup: 12 tenants, mix of 7B/13B/70B models, continuous batching with target batch latency 30ms and bursty arrival process (Pareto, alpha=1.5).
Primary metrics: OOM count, p95 token latency, per-token GPU cost, KV hit-rate, reclaimed_bytes/sec during compaction.
Baseline: static hard reserve strategy. Baseline OOMs: 43 in 12h; p95 latency 220ms; per-token cost baseline 1.00x.
Soft-watermark prototype: OOMs: 9 in 12h (-78%), p95 latency 238ms (+8%), per-token cost 1.03x. KV hit-rate dropped from 78%->64% under burst.
Goal tuning: target p95 latency increase <=5% while keeping OOM reduction >=60% via softer trim hysteresis and prioritized eviction policies.
notes: We will iterate parameter defaults over two canary clusters: canary-small (2xA100, mixed models) and canary-large (8xA100, high concurrency) before wide rollout.
Consider exposing a "burst_contract" flag in tenant config to allow premium tenants to reserve higher soft headroom for short windows (billing implications to be discussed with PM).
Follow-up: integrate with autoscaler to allow temporary weight prewarming when sustained contract usage exceeds threshold.
